steps.title: Node 24 is installed
steps.hint: Run `node -v` in a terminal. If it is older than v24, ask your mentor to update Node.

steps.title: Yarn 1 runs this command
steps.hint: Run `yarn -v`. It should print 1.22.something. Run the check with `yarn verify 00-setup`, not with npm.

steps.title: Dependencies are installed
steps.hint: Run `yarn install` in the bootcamp folder. If it cannot download packages, check your .npmrc (see 00-setup/README.md).

steps.title: The ticket API answers on port 8000
steps.hint: Start it in a second terminal with `python server/server.py` (or `py server/server.py`) and leave it running.

steps.title: copyTicket: a copy that does not share the original
steps.hint: Spread makes a new object: `{ ...ticket }`. Slide "Spread copies one level" shows why `const copy = ticket` is not a copy.

steps.title: closeTicket: a closed copy with closedAt
steps.hint: Spread first, then the fields that change: `{ ...ticket, status: ..., closedAt }`. Later keys win.

steps.title: ticketLabel: destructuring with defaults
steps.hint: Unpack in one line: `const { id, title = '(no title)', priority = 'medium' } = ticket;` then build a template string.

steps.title: toggleStatus: add or remove without mutating
steps.hint: Copy the outer object and build a new statuses array: `.filter()` to remove, `[...statuses, status]` to add. Never `.push()` or `.splice()`.

steps.title: replaceTicket: swap one item, keep the rest
steps.hint: `.map()` returns a new array. Return `updated` for the matching id and the same `t` for every other one.

steps.title: removeTicket: a new array without one item
steps.hint: `.filter()` keeps the items you return true for.

steps.title: sameContent: deep equality
steps.hint: Recursion: compare primitives with ===, then check both are arrays or both objects, compare key counts, and call sameContent on every key.

steps.title: deepFreeze: freeze every level
steps.hint: Loop over Object.values(value), call deepFreeze on each object inside, then Object.freeze(value).

steps.title: titles: map
steps.hint: `[t.title for t in tickets]` in Python is `tickets.map((t) => t.title)`.

steps.title: notClosed: filter
steps.hint: `tickets.filter((t) => ...)` keeps the items where the arrow returns true.

steps.title: findById: find
steps.hint: `.find()` returns the first match, or undefined when nothing matches.

steps.title: checkTickets: some and every
steps.hint: `.some()` is Python's any(), `.every()` is all(). Return both in one object.

steps.title: countByPriority: reduce into an object
steps.hint: Start reduce from `{ low: 0, medium: 0, high: 0, urgent: 0 }` and return a new object with one count increased. Slide "How reduce builds one value" walks through it.

steps.title: newestFirst: sort without mutating
steps.hint: Use `.toSorted()`, not `.sort()`. ISO dates compare as text: `b.createdAt.localeCompare(a.createdAt)`.

steps.title: indexById: Object.fromEntries
steps.hint: Make pairs first: `tickets.map((t) => [t.id, t])`, then turn the pairs into an object.

steps.title: hotList: chain the methods
steps.hint: filter (urgent or high, not closed), then toSorted (newest first), then slice(0, n), then map to titles. Slide "Chaining".

steps.title: groupBy: write it with reduce
steps.hint: For each item, compute its key, then return `{ ...groups, [key]: [...(groups[key] ?? []), item] }`.

steps.title: pipe: compose functions
steps.hint: `(x) => fns.reduce((value, fn) => fn(value), x)`.

steps.title: makeCounter: each counter keeps its own count
steps.hint: Each call to makeCounter creates a new local variable. Slide 'The backpack' shows where it lives.

steps.title: once: run a function only the first time
steps.hint: Keep two things in the backpack: whether fn already ran, and what it returned.

steps.title: memoize: cache results by argument
steps.hint: A Map in the closure works like a Python dict. Check with .has() before calling fn.

steps.title: createIdGenerator: ticket ids like T-1, T-2
steps.hint: Same pattern as makeCounter, plus a template string: `${prefix}-${n}`.

steps.title: debounce: wait until calls stop
steps.hint: Keep the timer id in the backpack. clearTimeout it on every call, then start a new one.

steps.title: wait: wrap setTimeout in a promise
steps.hint: `return new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));`

steps.title: predictOrder: the event loop
steps.hint: Normal code runs first, then promise callbacks, then timers. Slide "The event loop" plays it step by step.

steps.title: fetchTitle: await one request
steps.hint: `const response = await client.get(`/tickets/${id}`);` and the ticket is in `response.data`.

steps.title: fetchTicketOrNull: handle 404
steps.hint: Wrap the await in try / catch. In the catch, return null when `error.response?.status === 404`, otherwise `throw error`.

steps.title: fetchMany: requests in parallel
steps.hint: Start every request first (map ids to promises, no await inside), then `await Promise.all(promises)`. Slide "One after another, or all at once?"

steps.title: fetchSome: partial failures
steps.hint: `Promise.allSettled` never rejects. Each result has `status: 'fulfilled'` with `value`, or `'rejected'` with `reason`. Use the index to know which id failed.

steps.title: withTimeout: race a timer
steps.hint: `Promise.race([promise, a promise that rejects after ms])`.

steps.title: retry: try again on failure
steps.hint: A for loop from 1 to times with try / catch inside. Remember the last error and throw it after the loop.

steps.title: priorities.js: named exports
steps.hint: Write `export` in front of the const and the function. Only exported names can be imported; Python lets you import anything, JavaScript does not.

steps.title: format.js: import, and a default export
steps.hint: At the top: `import { PRIORITIES } from './priorities.js';` Then `export default function formatTicket(...)`. Slide "Named or default".

steps.title: dates.js: split a file in two
steps.hint: Create dates.js next to tickets.js, move the whole isOverdue function into it with `export` in front, then import it in tickets.js. Python does the same with a new .py file.

steps.title: index.js: re-export from one place
steps.hint: `export { PRIORITIES, comparePriority } from './priorities.js';` re-exports without importing first. A default export is re-exported with `export { default as formatTicket } from './format.js';`. Slide "One front door: index.js".

steps.title: counter.js: module state and live imports
steps.hint: `export let count = 0;` and a function that does `count += 1`. A module runs once, so every importer shares the same count. Slide "Imports are live".

steps.title: report.js: use the front door
steps.hint: Import comparePriority, formatTicket and overdueTickets from './index.js'. Then: overdue tickets → toSorted(comparePriority) → map(formatTicket).

steps.title: report.js: load a module on demand
steps.hint: `const module = await import('./format.js');` returns a promise of the module. The default export is `module.default`.

steps.title: api.js: load tickets and assignees
steps.hint: createClient returns `axios.create({ baseURL })`. The fetch functions await client.get(...) and return response.data. Module 01-js/04, steps 3 to 5.

steps.title: api.js: loadAll survives a server that is down
steps.hint: Use Promise.allSettled, which never rejects. For each result, check `status === 'fulfilled'` to pick its value or an empty list plus a warning.

steps.title: api.js: loadAll keeps tickets when assignees fail
steps.hint: Start both requests before awaiting anything: `await Promise.allSettled([fetchTickets(client), fetchAssignees(client)])`.

steps.title: filters.js: filter by status, priority, assignee, search
steps.hint: One filter call with a condition per field. Lowercase both the title and the search text before `.includes()`.

steps.title: filters.js: combined and empty filters
steps.hint: For each field: `(!status || t.status === status)`. An empty string is falsy, so it lets everything through. Trim the search text.

steps.title: filters.js: sort by date, priority or title, both ways
steps.hint: toSorted, never sort. Priority order is `PRIORITIES.indexOf(...)`. For descending, multiply the compare result by -1.

steps.title: stats.js: group by status, with empty groups
steps.hint: Start from STATUSES, not from the tickets: `Object.fromEntries(STATUSES.map((s) => [s, ...]))`.

steps.title: stats.js: total, open, overdue, average age
steps.hint: Compare dates as text: `t.dueDate < now.toISOString().slice(0, 10)`. Age in days: `Math.floor((now - new Date(t.createdAt)) / 86400000)`.

steps.title: validation.js: every error at once
steps.hint: Start with `const errors = []`, push one `{ field, message }` per broken rule (no early return), then return `{ valid: errors.length === 0, errors }`.

steps.title: Clean modules: no console, everything works through index.js
steps.hint: Remove any console.log from src/ (yarn tickets prints for you). Own imports need the extension: `./constants.js`.

steps.title: filters.js: sort by due date, missing dates last
steps.hint: Handle the null case before the direction: if only one ticket has no dueDate, it goes after the other whatever the direction.

modules.title: Why TypeScript, and how it runs

steps.title: daysOpen: type the parameters and the result
steps.hint: Write the type after each name with a colon: `(createdAt: string, now: Date): number`. Like Python's `def f(x: str) -> int`.

steps.title: shout: a typo TypeScript found
steps.hint: Hover the red underline and read the message: which property does not exist?

steps.title: titleOf: find may return undefined
steps.hint: `.find()` returns the ticket or undefined. Check `found` before using it, and return '(not found)' when it is missing.

steps.title: dueLabel: handle null before passing it on
steps.hint: dueDate is `string | null`, but formatDate only takes a string. Check for null first; after the check TypeScript knows it is a string.

steps.title: run-me.ts: what Node prints when types are wrong
steps.hint: Run `node 02-ts/01-why-ts/run-me.ts` in the bootcamp folder and copy the text after "Total hours:". Slide "Types disappear when the code runs".

steps.title: Assignee: an object type
steps.hint: `type Assignee = { id: string; name: string };` An object type lists each field and its type.

steps.title: Ticket: optional, readonly and nullable fields
steps.hint: `readonly id: string` cannot be reassigned; `description?: string` may be missing; `dueDate: string | null` is always there but may be null. Slide "Three kinds of maybe".

steps.title: createTicket: typed parameters and a default
steps.hint: A parameter with a default is optional: `priority = 'medium'`. Say what it returns: `): Ticket {`.

steps.title: ClosedTicket: an interface that extends Ticket
steps.hint: `export interface ClosedTicket extends Ticket { closedAt: string }`. Then return `{ ...ticket, status: 'closed', closedAt }`.

steps.title: addTicket: readonly arrays have no push
steps.hint: Return a new array with spread: `[...tickets, ticket]`. readonly is TypeScript's way of saying "do not mutate".

steps.title: TicketFilter: a function type
steps.hint: A function type looks like an arrow: `(ticket: Ticket) => boolean`. Once isOpen has that type, its parameter is typed for free.

steps.title: indexById: Record<string, Ticket>
steps.hint: `Record<string, Ticket>` is an object with string keys and Ticket values, like Python's dict[str, Ticket].

steps.title: Priority: a union of literal types
steps.hint: `type Priority = 'low' | 'medium' | ...;` Then read the new red underline on DEFAULT_PRIORITY.

steps.title: assigneeName: narrow undefined away
steps.hint: Two checks, two early returns: first for assigneeId === undefined, then for a find that found nothing. After each check TypeScript knows more.

steps.title: toTicketId: narrow with typeof
steps.hint: `typeof id === 'number'` works like Python's isinstance(id, int). Inside the if, id is a number; after it, a string.

steps.title: describeResult: narrow with in
steps.hint: `'error' in result` tells the two shapes apart. Slide "Four ways to narrow".

steps.title: errorMessage: narrow unknown with instanceof
steps.hint: unknown allows nothing until you check it. `error instanceof Error` first, then `typeof error === 'string'`.

steps.title: priorityRank: switch over a union
steps.hint: One case per priority. If every case returns, TypeScript knows the function always returns a number.

steps.title: parsePriority: from text to a Priority without as
steps.hint: Normalise the text, then `PRIORITIES.find((p) => p === wanted)`: find on a Priority[] returns Priority | undefined.

steps.title: isPriority: a type predicate
steps.hint: Change `: boolean` to `: value is Priority`. Compare without `as`: `PRIORITIES.some((p) => p === value)`.

steps.title: isRecord: an object you can read
steps.hint: Three checks: typeof value === 'object', value !== null (typeof null is 'object'!), and !Array.isArray(value).

steps.title: isAssignee: build guards from guards
steps.hint: After `isRecord(value) &&`, TypeScript lets you read value.id and value.name as unknown. Check each with typeof.

steps.title: isTicket: every field, the right type
steps.hint: One && chain: isRecord, then one check per field. Write a small isStatus like isPriority. dueDate is `=== null` or a string.

steps.title: assertTicket: throw instead of returning false
steps.hint: Return type `asserts value is Ticket`. Inside: `if (!isTicket(value)) throw new Error(...)`. Slide "Guard or assert?".

steps.title: parseTickets: keep the valid ones
steps.hint: `if (!Array.isArray(data)) throw new Error(...)`. Then `data.filter(isTicket)` gives a Ticket[], because isTicket is a type guard. invalid is the difference in length.

steps.title: ticketProblems: say what is wrong
steps.hint: Same checks as isTicket, but push a message for each failure instead of stopping at the first.

steps.title: Ticket: one type per status, joined in a union
steps.hint: Add the extra fields to each of the four types, then `export type Ticket = OpenTicket | AssignedTicket | BlockedTicket | ClosedTicket;` Slide "One type per state".

steps.title: statusLabel: switch on the discriminant
steps.hint: `switch (ticket.status)`. Inside `case 'blocked':` TypeScript knows ticket is a BlockedTicket, so ticket.blockedReason is allowed.

steps.title: statusLabel: exhaustive with never
steps.hint: Add `default: return assertNever(ticket);`. When every status has a case, ticket is `never` there; a new status makes it an error.

steps.title: assign: open in, assigned out
steps.hint: `return { ...ticket, status: 'assigned', assignee };` The return type checks you added everything an AssignedTicket needs.

steps.title: close: build from the base fields
steps.hint: Destructure the base fields out of ticket, then add status, closedAt and (when the ticket has one) assignee. Spreading the whole ticket would carry blockedReason along.

steps.title: assigneeOf: read a field only some states have
steps.hint: `ticket.status === 'open' ? undefined : ticket.assignee` narrows the union to the three states that have assignee.

steps.title: first<T>: a generic function
steps.hint: Add `<T>` after the name and use T for the items and the result: `first<T>(items: readonly T[]): T | undefined`. Slide "A type parameter".

steps.title: indexBy<T>: generic callbacks
steps.hint: Use T in both places: `items: readonly T[]` and `keyOf: (item: T) => string`, and return Record<string, T>.

steps.title: TicketDraft, TicketChanges, TicketSummary from Ticket
steps.hint: `Omit<Ticket, 'id' | 'createdAt'>`, `Partial<TicketDraft>`, `Pick<Ticket, 'id' | 'title'>`. Slide "Utility types".

steps.title: updateTicket: apply a Partial
steps.hint: Spread the ticket, then the changes, then put id and createdAt back from the original ticket.

steps.title: summarize: Pick at run time
steps.hint: Types do not remove fields at run time. Build the object yourself: `{ id: ticket.id, title: ticket.title }`.

steps.title: Result<T>: a generic union
steps.hint: Two members with a literal ok: `{ ok: true; data: T } | { ok: false; error: string }`. Then `result.ok ? result.data : fallback`.

steps.title: countBy<T, K extends string>
steps.hint: A second type parameter for the key: `K extends string`, and the callback returns K. The result is Partial<Record<K, number>>.

steps.title: Status type derived from the STATUSES array
steps.hint: Without help, TypeScript widens the array to string[]. The lesson's slide 'Freeze the values' shows how to keep the exact strings, then how to read a union out of an array type.

steps.title: PRIORITY_LABELS checked with satisfies
steps.hint: `satisfies Record<Priority, string>` checks every key without widening the values.

steps.title: statusOptions: dropdown options typed from Status
steps.hint: Build the options from STATUSES instead of writing them out. If value comes out as string, look at what type STATUSES has and what map returns.

steps.title: TicketField: the keys of a ticket, as a type
steps.hint: keyof works on a type. Which type describes a ticket here?

steps.title: @ts-check: let TypeScript read the JavaScript
steps.hint: Put `// @ts-check` as the first line of report.js and hover the red underline. Python's round(x, 1) has no JavaScript twin: round x * 10, then divide by 10.

steps.title: Rename report.js to report.ts
steps.hint: Rename the file in VS Code (F2 on it in the explorer). Behaviour must stay the same; the red underlines are next step's job.

steps.title: Zero type errors under strict
steps.hint: Import the types: `import { isTicket, type Ticket } from './types.ts';` Type each parameter; client is `AxiosInstance` (import type from 'axios').

steps.title: No any, no as, no !, no @ts-ignore
steps.hint: Each of these hides a question TypeScript asked. Answer it with a real type or a check instead.

steps.title: fetchReport: check what the API sends
steps.hint: `client.get<unknown>('/tickets')`, then keep only `data.filter(isTicket)` when data is an array. Return type: Promise<string[]>.

steps.title: PRIORITY_WEIGHT: as const satisfies
steps.hint: Export it and end the object with `as const satisfies Record<Priority, number>`. Module 07, step 2.

modules.title: Phase 2 project: ticket logic in strict TypeScript

steps.title: Every file is .ts
steps.hint: Run `yarn copy-project` once, then rename each file in 02-ts/project/src to .ts and change the imports to './constants.ts' and so on.

steps.title: tsc strict: zero errors
steps.hint: Work file by file in the order of README.md. Hover each red underline; module 02-ts/08 is the same workflow.

steps.title: No any, as, ! or @ts-ignore
steps.hint: Each shortcut hides a question. Use a type guard, a narrowing check or a real type instead. `as const` is allowed.

steps.title: STATUSES and PRIORITIES as const, types derived
steps.hint: `export const STATUSES = [...] as const; export type Status = (typeof STATUSES)[number];` Module 02-ts/07.

steps.title: Ticket is a discriminated union
steps.hint: One type per status, joined with |. Put them in a new src/types.ts and re-export it from index.ts. Module 02-ts/05.

steps.title: statusLabel: exhaustive switch with never
steps.hint: Bring statusLabel and assertNever from module 02-ts/05 into your project and export them.

steps.title: API data checked by a type guard
steps.hint: `client.get<unknown>(...)`, then isTicket on every item. Count the malformed ones and add a warning in loadAll that names their ids.

steps.title: Everything from Phase 1 still works
steps.hint: The message names the Phase 1 step that broke. Run `yarn tickets`: it now runs your TypeScript version.

steps.title: Due-date sort still works
steps.hint: Phase 1 step 11, now typed: tickets without a dueDate go last.

steps.title: useToggle: a boolean with a toggle function
steps.hint: A custom hook is a function that calls other hooks. Start from useState.

steps.title: useDebouncedValue: the value, once it stops changing
steps.hint: useEffect with a setTimeout, and return a cleanup that clears it. Which values belong in the dependency array?

steps.title: SearchBox: report the search only after typing stops
steps.hint: Keep the text in state, pass it through useDebouncedValue, and call onSearch from an effect on the debounced value.

steps.title: usePrevious: the value from the last render
steps.hint: A ref survives renders without causing one. Update it in an effect.

steps.title: Every file in src is .ts or .tsx
steps.hint: Rename one file at a time and fix the errors tsc reports before moving on.

steps.title: tsc --noEmit passes with strict: true
steps.hint: Run `yarn tsc -p final-project` to see the errors with file and line.

steps.title: ESLint passes with the React Hooks rules
steps.hint: Run `yarn eslint final-project` to see each rule that fails.

steps.title: Bug: sorting must not change the cached tickets
steps.hint: Rules of React: never mutate data you did not create. Which array methods change the array in place?

steps.title: Performance: search filters only after typing stops
steps.hint: Your useDebouncedValue hook from 03-react/04, plus useMemo so the filtered list is not rebuilt on every render.

steps.title: Feature: assignee filter kept in the URL
steps.hint: useSearchParams from react-router-dom reads and writes ?assignee=a2.
